summary: When an IPv6 packet is sent to a multicast address on Ethernet, the address is normally mapped to an Ethernet multicast address. This standards-track document clarifies that in some circumstances the packet may instead be sent to an Ethernet unicast address. It updates RFC 2464.

plainLanguage.summary: Usually a message for a whole group goes out on a loudspeaker. This note says that sometimes it is fine to hand the message to just one person instead.

can ipv6 multicast use an ethernet unicast address
subtitle: Clarifies that an IPv6 multicast packet may be sent in an Ethernet unicast frame when only one receiver matters.

tldr.problem: RFC 2464 maps an IPv6 multicast destination address to an Ethernet multicast address, leaving unclear whether a unicast Ethernet address is allowed.
tldr.mechanism: This document explicitly allows mapping an IPv6 multicast packet to an Ethernet unicast address when it is clear that only one address is relevant, and requires receivers not to drop such packets.
tldr.outcome: It extends the RFC 2464 mapping without replacing it, and updates RFC 2464.

today: RFC 6085 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 2464. No later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Section 7 of RFC 2464 says how an IPv6 packet with a multicast destination address is mapped to an Ethernet link-layer address. This document extends that mapping to explicitly allow an Ethernet unicast address, when it is clear that only one address is relevant.

The new mapping does not replace the RFC 2464 one. How the unicast Ethernet address is determined, and how the outgoing IPv6 packet is built, are out of scope.
sections.plainLanguage: Group messages normally go to the group's mailbox. Now they may go to one person's mailbox if only that person needs them.

sections.title: Receiving Such Packets
sections.content: The one rule is for receivers: an IPv6 node that receives a packet with a multicast destination address and an Ethernet link-layer unicast address MUST NOT drop the packet because of this form of address mapping.
sections.plainLanguage: If a group message arrives addressed to you alone, do not throw it away just for that.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document states that it does not introduce any new security vulnerabilities. It offers no further analysis.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new that could go wrong was found.

references.text: Crawford, M., "Transmission of IPv6 Packets over Ethernet Networks", RFC 2464, December 1998.
